metadata.title: Efficient Computation of Positional Population Counts Using SIMD Instructions

extraction_notes.note: The C++ listings in figures (CSA, CSA_AVX512, the 256 B and 1 kB circuits, the scalar baseline, the vectorized increment, and the inline scalar loop) are code, not prose; they were not made nodes. The algorithms they implement are the prose algorithm nodes AP3-AP6.
The experimental evidence is a table of cycles, instructions and GB/s per input size (tab:results) and a speed figure; only the findings stated in prose became numerical claims.

The abstract and the conclusion restate the problem, the speedups and the near-memcpy speed; per one node per repeated statement they got no node. The headline speedup factor is inconsistent across copies: 50-fold (abstract, intro), over 40 times (conclusion); instruction reduction 400 times (abstract, 4.1) vs 300 times measured (ClP22).

PP2 has index typos: it calls $B_0,\ldots,B_N$ the first $N$ outputs and writes the following inputs as $d_N,\ldots$ (should start at $d_{2^N}$). AP5 says it uses the 256 B circuit but feeds 512 B blocks and reads a fourth register B3, which matches the 512 B circuit.

AP3 is introduced as an illustration ('Let us illustrate this approach'), so it could be an example; chose algorithm because it is a stepwise procedure. PP2 is a recursive circuit construction that could be an algorithm; chose proof because it is the argument for ClP6.
An empirical performance statement of prior work (Mula et al.) stated in full; typed theorem/external per the cited-result rule though claim would read more naturally.

nodes.statement: For simplicity let us assume that we are working with the smaller circuit (256\,B). Before starting the procedure, the registers B0, B1, B2 and the 16 output bit-counters are zero-initialized. Next, the first 512\,B of inputs are process with the circuit and receive as output the updated values of B0, B1, B2. In addition, we also receive a new register B3 corresponding to the fourth least significant bit of the sum of the set bits at position iin [0,1,ldots, 512). We can update our sixteen bit-counters by checking the bits in B3: the first counter needs to be incremented by eight times the sum of the bits at indexes \0, 16, 32, ldots, 496\, the second counter needs to be incremented by eight times the sum of the bits at indexes \1, 17, 33, ldots, 497\, and so forth. The process of loading the next 512\,B of input data, call the circuit, and providing it with the updated values B0, B1, B2 is repeated until no more data is available. At this point, when no more input data is available, we must increment our bit-counters with the remaining bits in B0, B1, B2. These are processed as B3 except that the multiplier is 1, 2 and 4 respectively.
nodes.raw_latex:
For simplicity let us assume that we are working with the smaller circuit (256\,B). Before starting the procedure, the registers \texttt{B0}, \texttt{B1}, \texttt{B2} and the 16 output bit-counters are zero-initialized. Next, the first 512\,B of inputs are process with the circuit and receive as output the updated values of \texttt{B0}, \texttt{B1}, \texttt{B2}. In addition, we also receive a new register \texttt{B3} corresponding to the fourth least significant bit of the sum of the set bits at position $i\in [0,1,\ldots, 512)$. We can update our sixteen bit-counters by checking the bits in \texttt{B3}: the first counter needs to be incremented by eight times the sum of the bits at indexes $\{0, 16, 32, \ldots, 496\}$, the second counter needs to be 
incremented by eight times the sum of the bits at indexes $\{1, 17, 33, \ldots, 497\}$, and so forth. The process of loading the next 512\,B of input data, call the circuit, and providing it with the updated values \texttt{B0}, \texttt{B1}, \texttt{B2} is repeated until no more data is available. At this point, when no more input data is available, we must increment our bit-counters with the remaining bits in \texttt{B0}, \texttt{B1}, \texttt{B2}. These are processed as \texttt{B3} except that the multiplier is 1, 2 and 4 respectively.

nodes.statement: Taken together, we introduce a novel population count operation referred to as the positional population count (pospopcnt) and introduce efficient SIMD-accelerated algorithms based on carry-saver add (CSA) circuits.
nodes.raw_latex:
Taken together, we introduce a novel population count operation referred to as
the \textit{positional population count} (\texttt{pospopcnt}) and introduce efficient SIMD-accelerated algorithms based on carry-saver add (CSA) circuits.
nodes.clean_text: Taken together, we introduce a novel population count operation referred to as the positional population count (pospopcnt) and introduce efficient SIMD-accelerated algorithms based on carry-saver add (CSA) circuits.
